caption: The fleet-wide LLM control plane: every request to every model, local or cloud, counted in one place.

callouts.label: Fleet totals
callouts.text: Every call to every model is counted in one place.

callouts.label: Cache hit rate
callouts.text: Shows how much input was reused from a prompt cache.

callouts.label: Dead models
callouts.text: Flags models that never once succeeded so they can leave the fallback chain.

callouts.label: Token mix
callouts.text: Splits traffic into prompt, completion and reasoning tokens.

caption: Traffic over time grouped by provider, so every token traces back to the backend that served it.

callouts.label: Traffic over time
callouts.text: Each line shows how work shifts between local and cloud providers day by day.

callouts.label: Attribution
callouts.text: Every series is a named backend, so each token can be traced to where it ran.

caption: The failures view: providers that never worked in the window, with the error and the last time they were seen. Machine names are blurred.

callouts.label: Dead providers
callouts.text: Providers that never once succeeded are listed first, with a plain instruction: remove from chain.

callouts.label: Why it failed
callouts.text: Fail rate, number of attempts and the actual error, side by side.

callouts.label: Verdict
callouts.text: Dead means it never worked; degraded means it fails some of the time.

caption: Live inference capacity: how much GPU and unified memory is free across the fleet right now.

callouts.label: One bar per GPU
callouts.text: Each bar is a graphics card, filled to show how much memory is in use.

callouts.label: Free memory
callouts.text: Green cards still have room for another model; red cards are full.

callouts.label: Unified memory
callouts.text: The Apple machine shares one memory pool, shown as a single bar.

callouts.label: Honest gaps
callouts.text: A machine that cannot be reached is shown as unreachable instead of being hidden.

caption: Everything the Karakuri software factory has built from plain-language requests: code, documents and apps in many languages, each marked delivered or needs attention.

callouts.label: Filter
callouts.text: Narrow hundreds of builds by name, by date range, or by whether they were delivered.

callouts.label: One card per build
callouts.text: Each card shows the kind of output, the file count, the language and the result.

callouts.label: Delivered
callouts.text: A green tag means the build passed its checks and shipped.

callouts.label: Many languages
callouts.text: Go, Python, Kotlin, C++, Java and more, all produced by the same factory.

caption: Ladder, the reading ladder: things read in become ideas, then tested hypotheses, experiments and finally algorithms, with a kill rate that shows whether triage is working.

callouts.label: Six stages
callouts.text: Sources become ideas, hypotheses, experiments, algorithms and results.

callouts.label: Ideas
callouts.text: Most items start as drafts. Few are promoted, and some are killed on purpose.

callouts.label: Conversion
callouts.text: Shows how many ideas survive each step of the ladder.

callouts.label: Kill rate
callouts.text: A healthy pipeline kills ideas often. That means triage is working.

caption: The fleet health page: checks that the things producing data are still producing it, not just still running. Machine names are blurred.

callouts.label: Freshness, not just uptime
callouts.text: Each check asks whether the output is still fresh, so silent failures show up.

callouts.label: Plain summary
callouts.text: One line says how many of the checks are failing.

callouts.label: Green means fresh
callouts.text: A green card means the backup or index was updated on schedule.

callouts.label: Red explains itself
callouts.text: A failing card says exactly what drifted and by how much.

caption: Fleet Desk: a single-pane daily desk where scored reading is ranked and each item can be researched, written up or dismissed.

callouts.label: Six views
callouts.text: Briefing, patterns, top finds, kept, interests and queue, all from one page.

callouts.label: Daily rebuild
callouts.text: The desk is rebuilt each day, ranking the new finds into must-see, high and worth a look.

callouts.label: One-click actions
callouts.text: Research sends an agent to dig in. Write sends it to be written up. Dismiss clears it.

callouts.label: Plain-language instructions
callouts.text: Or type what you want done instead, in ordinary words.

caption: The agent office: AI agents drawn as small office workers moving between rooms. Names in the status panel are blurred.

callouts.label: Break room
callouts.text: Agents that are idle or not reporting are drawn here.

callouts.label: The bridge
callouts.text: The main floor, drawn as an office with desks.

callouts.label: Honest status
callouts.text: The panel separates 'not working' from 'unmeasured', so missing data is not hidden.

callouts.label: Machinery
callouts.text: Counts the services that are running against the ones actually doing work.

caption: Podcast Studio: every show the desk produces, grouped by network. One show title is blurred.

callouts.label: Top controls
callouts.text: Generate an episode, see stats, edit global settings or open the voice pool.

callouts.label: Networks
callouts.text: Each brand is a network that holds its own shows.

callouts.label: Show templates
callouts.text: Forty show formats, from solo and duo to panel, debate and quiz.

caption: Studio stats: real production timing pulled from each episode's own record, with no estimates.

callouts.label: Real timings
callouts.text: Episodes produced, average and median time, and daily throughput.

callouts.label: Where the time goes
callouts.text: Click a stage to see which episodes ran slowest there.

callouts.label: Audio dominates
callouts.text: Making the audio takes about half of the total time.

caption: Daemon: a public, machine-readable broadcast of what is being built and thought about. The location field is blurred.

callouts.label: Live status strip
callouts.text: A running clock, last sync and section count show the page is alive.

callouts.label: Live feed
callouts.text: The latest code pushes and articles, merged into one stream.

callouts.label: Mission
callouts.text: A short statement of what the work is for.

callouts.label: Telos
callouts.text: The principles and goals the whole broadcast is built around.

caption: Unwatched, a self-hosted island town of AI citizens that keeps living while you are away. One shop name is blurred.

callouts.label: Send someone over
callouts.text: You put a person on the island and they make their own decisions.

callouts.label: Residents
callouts.text: Townspeople going about their day on a drawn street map.

callouts.label: Live ticker
callouts.text: A running log of what is happening in town right now.

callouts.label: Mini-map
callouts.text: A small overview of the whole island.

caption: The public fleet map: GPU boxes, the models on each card and the memory they use. Machine names are blurred.

callouts.label: Capacity at a glance
callouts.text: Total memory, how much is committed, how much is free and how much is held in reserve.

callouts.label: One group per machine
callouts.text: Each machine lists its cards and how full they are.

callouts.label: Card and model
callouts.text: Every GPU shows its memory bar and the model pinned to it.

callouts.label: Held in reserve
callouts.text: Dashed boxes are capacity kept free for bursts of voice work.

caption: The Fleet Dispatch daily briefing as it arrives by email, showing the Technology section of one edition.

callouts.label: Masthead
callouts.text: A daily briefing, assembled and sent by email each morning.

callouts.label: Sections
callouts.text: Stories are grouped by topic, and this one is the Technology section.

callouts.label: Top stories
callouts.text: The lead stories get a short summary and a link to the source.

callouts.label: The rest
callouts.text: Everything else is a headline and a line, with the source named.

caption: A generated realm map for an AI-run tabletop adventure: kingdoms, borders and a title, all drawn by the map generator.

callouts.label: Titled map
callouts.text: Every adventure gets its own named map.

callouts.label: Generated realms
callouts.text: Coastlines, borders and rivers are generated, not hand drawn.

callouts.label: Named kingdoms
callouts.text: Each realm is labelled, so the game master can refer to places by name.

callouts.label: Scale bar
callouts.text: A scale in kilometres keeps distances believable.

caption: A generated walled-city map from the adventure builder, with named districts, harbour, docks and a castle.

callouts.label: Walls and gates
callouts.text: The city is drawn with a defensive wall and gatehouses.

callouts.label: Named districts
callouts.text: Wards and docks are labelled so scenes can be set in a specific place.

callouts.label: Castle
callouts.text: Key locations from the story are placed on the map.

callouts.label: Compass
callouts.text: North is marked so directions in the narration line up.

caption: An illustrated battle map generated for a combat scene: an entrance, a central brazier and scattered cover.

callouts.label: Entrance
callouts.text: The way in is drawn clearly so players know where the fight starts.

callouts.label: Centre of the room
callouts.text: A landmark in the middle gives the combat a focal point.

callouts.label: Cover
callouts.text: Statues and rubble give characters something to hide behind.

callouts.label: Second exit
callouts.text: Stairs and a side door give the fight more than one direction.

caption: A stylized dungeon map with numbered rooms, a legend and a scale bar, built for the game master to read from.

callouts.label: Title
callouts.text: The map is named after the adventure it belongs to.

callouts.label: Numbered rooms
callouts.text: Rooms match the numbers in the adventure text.

callouts.label: Legend
callouts.text: Doors, water, stairs and statues are explained in a key.

callouts.label: Scale bar
callouts.text: One square is five feet, so movement and range can be judged.
